newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HUD's Cisneros sends resignation to Clinton.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HUD's Cisneros sends resignation to Clinton.

text.p: U.S. Housing Secretary Henry Cisneros submitted his resignation Thursday, the latest cabinet member to quit ahead of President Bill Clinton's second term.
"I have concluded that I cannot ask to be considered for service in the next four years," Cisneros wrote in his resignation letter to Clinton.
"The president thanks Secretary Cisneros for the outstanding work he's done at HUD and for being a good friend," Barry Toiv, a White House spokesman, said.
Cisneros had long been expected to leave his position and said earlier Thursday that a key deciding factor would be whether he could financially afford to stay on.
"I've been wrestling with this question about whether or not I could afford to stay," he said.

A leading candidate to replace Cisneros is Atlanta Mayor Bill Campbell who has discussed the job with Clinton's transition team. Another possible contender is Andrew Cuomo, assistant secretary at the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
